summary: No held thesis is broken by evidence in the files. Every held single stock is still on the 11-17 menu, and no new 10-K, flag or failed test appeared for any of them. The day's -$5.58 came mostly from price, not from fundamentals: MCO -4.32% and MSCI -4.20% fell together, CARG -3.17% and IDXX -1.49%, while DPZ rose 1.0%. One down day cannot break a quality thesis. The only buy, SAM ($15 at $220.14), was my rank 7 and went in with the concerns I gave it (thin net income against $1,965M revenue, current_ratio_improved fails, FY2025 data). No Reviewer lesson names this role and I have no graded calls, so none shaped this review. I used L3 and L6 evidence only for the sleeve and stop-text notes below.
update: 1) MCO/MSCI: the morning note called their shared leverage_not_up failure a concern for the sleeve as a whole. Today they moved as one sleeve, both down about 4.2-4.3% (about 8.1% of equity together). That is one day and not graded evidence, but it backs sizing them as one position under L3. Their fundamentals have not changed (MCO F8, CFO $2.90B vs NI $2.46B; MSCI F8, CFO $1.59B vs NI $1.20B). MCO is now the nearest single-stock stop at 3.07% above $470, closer than EXEL at 5.38% above $65. The PM's morning line that 'EXEL is closest' is out of date after the close. 2) SAM: the stored text still measures $201 as 'about 10% under the $223.29 menu close'. The fill was $220.14, so $201 is about 8.7% under the fill. Under L6 the PM should restate it from the fill at the next run. The fundamentals case is unchanged, and the 'screen drops SAM' clause has not tripped (SAM is still on the menu at gp_sector_pct 0.945). 3) Staples by SIC label is now DPZ, WMT, KR and SAM, about 28% of equity (bucket, excluding DPZ, about 16.6%), going into WMT's confirmed 11-19 print. That print is the first fresh fundamental test for a held Staples name, since WMT's data is FY ended 2026-01-31. 4) FAST stays F8 with CFO $1,296M vs NI $1,258M, the thinnest cash cover among the held names. It is the PM's named first single-stock cut, and I agree on the fundamentals. 5) Unchanged watch items for the next ranking: FTDR (F9, rank 4) and TPR (F8, rank 5) are the best unheld names. TTEK's new 10-K (known_since 11-17, the shadow bought it today) fails leverage_not_up and asset_turnover_improved. VOO and VTI cannot appear on the menu, so they have no fundamental test, and their risk sits entirely on the SPY 200-day stop, now NEAR at +0.39%.
